T.G. Shivashankare Gowda, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal, the appellant has challenged the judgment dated 25.02.2021 passed in MVC No.1064 of 2018 on the file of the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XII, Vijayapura (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).
2. The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Briefly stated the facts are that, petitioner is the mother of Maruthi, the deceased.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XII, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The deceased was injured in a road accident that took place on 02-08-2018 at Canal Bridge on Kakhandki-Uppaldinni Road, Vijayapura, hit by Tractor bearing Engine No. ZJM2TAP3077 and Chassis No.MBNBEBBBAJZM00663 against his Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-28/ES- 3429 from the opposite direction.

The deceased died on 07-08-2018 at Yashodhara Hospital,
Solapur.
Petitioner being the mother has claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
She pleaded that deceased was aged 23 years, working as driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.9,64,000/- with 6% interest.

4. The petitioner is before this court pleading inadequacy in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, income taken is on the lower side, future prospects was not considered, so also the compensation towards conventional heads is not proportionate to the settled principles.

5. Heard the arguments of Sri.Sanganagouda V.Biradar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Sanjay M Joshi, learned counsel for Insurance Company.
6.

It is the contention of learned counsel for petitioner, the deceased was though earning Rs.20,000/- per month, Tribunal has taken only Rs.8,000/-, he was a professional driver, future prospects was not taken into consideration, the award amount towards conventional heads is not in Kamalabai W/O Lachchappa vs Hanamant And Anr on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2430438/
2 consonance with the settled principles and accordingly, he sought for re-assessment and enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Kamalabai W/O Lachchappa vs Hanamant And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company contended that the Tribunal correctly assessed the income of the deceased as the accident was of the year 2018, the compensation under conventional heads has been settled and accordingly compensation may be assessed and supported the impugned judgment.
8. We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.

9. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of the deceased in the accident,
the petitioner being the mother as dependent is entitled to claim compensation.

Though it is claimed that the deceased was a professional driver, it is not established by placing his driving licence and where he was working, in the absence of such proof, the deceased has to be considered as a person with no proof of income.
The accident was in the year 2018, the Tribunal considered the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.
Having regard to the evidence and the year of accident, it is on the lower side and it ought to have been assessed minimum of Rs.11,750/- per month.
Hence, we assess the income of the deceased accordingly.
10. As seen from the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has not considered the future prospects and also the conventional heads.

By applying the principles laid down in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680, future prospects should be taken as 40% for age below 40 years for a person who has no permanent job.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.P3/Postmortem report confirms that the deceased was aged 23 years.
Hence, applicable multiplier as per decision of Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. DTC- (2009)6 SCC 121, is '18'.

The deceased died during the treatment, for which, the petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.25,000/-
and that amount needs to be reimbursed.

11. If all these factors are taken into consideration the assessment of loss of dependency would be:
Rs.11,750/- (Income of the deceased) + Rs.4,700/- (40% future prospects) =
Rs.16,450/- per month.
The deceased was a bachelor, 50% has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Accordingly, the calculation towards loss of dependency is Rs.16,450/- - Rs.8,225/- = Rs.8,225/- x 12= Rs.98,700/- x 18 multiplier = Rs.17,76,600/-.
Under the conventional heads, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection, towards loss of estate and funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- each is assessed.
Towards medical expenses Rs.25,000/- is assessed.

Then the total compensation comes to Rs.17,76,600/- + Rs.70,000/- + Rs.25,000/- =
Rs.18,71,600/-, which is the just compensation to which the petitioner is entitled.
The appeal filed by the petitioner deserves to be allowed in part by modifying the compensation from Rs.9,64,000/- to Rs.18,71,600/-, by enhancing the amount to the tune of Rs.9,07,600/-.
